hook.line: When you agree with someone at a meeting, you want to say exactly what you agree on. *Coincidir* does that, and it is also how Spanish says two things happen at the same time.
hook.es: Coincido contigo en que el problema es el transporte.
hook.en: I agree with you that the problem is transport.

examples.es: Coincido contigo en que el problema es el transporte.
examples.en: I agree with you that the problem is transport.

examples.es: Vale coincide con Tomás en que el café es importante.
examples.en: Vale agrees with Tomás that the café is important.

examples.es: Coincido con usted en lo principal.
examples.en: I agree with you on the main point.

examples.es: Ayer coincidí con Mariana en el banco.
examples.en: Yesterday I ran into Mariana at the bank.

rule:
*Coincidir con* + person + *en* + what you agree on: *Coincido contigo en…*. For a whole idea use *en que*: *en que el problema es el transporte*.

Watch the pieces: *con* + person (*contigo*, *conmigo*, *con usted*), then *en*. Never *de*.
With *nosotros*, drop the person: *Coincidimos en casi todo*.
Things can coincide too: *Nuestros horarios coinciden*.
And meeting someone by chance is *coincidir* as well.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb with a fixed preposition: *coincidir* always travels with *con* for the person and *en* for the point.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Coincido ___ en que el problema es el transporte.* (*contigo* or *con ti*) I agree with you (a friend) that the problem is transport.
yourTurn.answer: Coincido contigo en que el problema es el transporte.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Coincidimos ___ casi todo.* (*en* or *de*) We agree on almost everything.
yourTurn.why: What you agree on always follows *en*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I agree with you (a friend) that the problem is transport.
yourTurn.answer: Coincido contigo en que el problema es el transporte.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale agrees with Tomás that the café is important.
yourTurn.answer: Vale coincide con Tomás en que el café es importante.
yourTurn.why: The person comes after *con*, the idea after *en que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I agree with you (formal) on the main point.
yourTurn.answer: Coincido con usted en lo principal.
yourTurn.why: *Usted* needs the full *con usted*, since *contigo* is only for *tú*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Yesterday I ran into Mariana at the bank.
yourTurn.answer: Ayer coincidí con Mariana en el banco.
yourTurn.why: A chance meeting uses *coincidir con* plus the place with *en*.

yourTurn.prompt: Change to *we*: *Coincido contigo en casi todo.*
yourTurn.why: With *nosotros* the other person is already included, so *contigo* goes.

pitfalls.wrong: Coincido con ti en que el problema es el transporte.
pitfalls.right: Coincido contigo en que el problema es el transporte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *con*, *ti* turns into one word: *contigo*.

pitfalls.wrong: Coincido contigo que el problema es el transporte.
pitfalls.right: Coincido contigo en que el problema es el transporte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English drops the preposition, but Spanish needs *en* before *que*.
Almost. *Coincidir* already means "agree", so *de acuerdo* is not added.

personal: Think of a friend and something you both feel strongly about. Say it: *Coincido con… en que…*.
